title: Rebooting AI
subtitle: Building Artificial Intelligence We Can Trust
pitch: Two scientists argue deep learning alone will not give us AI we can trust, and that we need common sense, reasoning and knowledge.

chapters.g: The gap between what AI seems to do and what it really understands.
Why untrustworthy AI is dangerous in cars, medicine and the courts.
What deep learning is good at and where it fails.

chapters.t: If computers are so smart, how come they can't read?
chapters.g: Reading needs understanding of the world, which current systems lack.
Why helpful home robots are still far away.
Lessons from cognitive science for building better AI.

chapters.t: Common sense, and the path to deep understanding
chapters.g: Building knowledge of time, space and causality into AI.
What it would take for AI to deserve our trust.

ideas: Deep learning alone is not enough for trustworthy AI.
Common sense is the missing ingredient.
Hybrid systems with reasoning and knowledge are needed.

args.a: Scaling deep learning will not reach general intelligence.
args.c: Supporters of scaling point to large language models' progress since 2019.

questions: Have large language models proved Marcus and Davis wrong, right, or both?
What would 'common sense' look like in a machine?

quiz.q: What do the authors say is missing from AI?
quiz.w: They argue for common sense reasoning.

o: A home robot from The Jetsons
quiz.w: The chapter asks why home robots like Rosie do not exist yet.
